text:
Dylan Larkin's first game as a Canadien had most of what his long autumn had been missing: real minutes, a forecheck that set up a goal, and a third star. It did not have a win, because Darcy Kuemper made 29 saves and the Kings left Centre Bell with a 2-1 victory.

The context matters. Larkin spent the start of this season refusing to play in Detroit until he was traded, and the deal that sent him to Montreal on Nov. 22 ended one of the stranger stories in years. He started Monday centring Alex Newhook and Alexandre Texier, per Arpon Basu's warmup lines, and it was his forecheck that produced the Canadiens' only goal, Newhook's snap shot at 7:28 of the second, as Karine Hains noted.

Montreal had the better of the play. The Canadiens took 70 shot attempts to 45, won the even-strength chances 2.31 to 1.43 in expected goals, and deserved to win 60% of the replays of this game's shots. Kuemper saved 1.46 goals more than expected, including a stop on Florian Xhekaj in the third, and added the most wins of anyone on the ice.

Los Angeles made its few chances count. Alex Laferriere scored a between-the-legs power-play goal in the first, with Quinton Byfield picking up his 200th career point on the assist. Trevor Moore's snap shot at 14:57 of the second, on an 8% chance, stood up as the winner after Montreal challenged it for goalie interference and lost, as Hains noted. The Kings went 1 for 1 on the power play and held Montreal to 0 for 3.

For the Canadiens, it is a night to file under process: a new second-line centre who looked like himself, with Chris Kreider out six to eight weeks and their depth stretched. For the Kings, Kuemper's form is the story worth watching as Kevin Fiala works back into the lineup.
headline: Larkin debuts in Montreal, Kuemper spoils the party
